It also includes two functions: `stockLevel`, which evaluates whether an item's quantity is below a threshold (less than 5), returning either `'low'` or `'ok'` [S2], and `stockValue`, which computes the total value of an item's stock by multiplying its price (from `pricing.ts`) by its quantity [S2].

This file is central because it provides the `Item` type and the `stockLevel` function, both of which are used by other files. Specifically, `pricing.ts` imports `stockLevel` from `inventory.ts` to determine whether to apply a scarcity surcharge when calculating the price of an item [S1]. Meanwhile, `report.ts` uses both `stockLevel` and `stockValue` to generate a formatted report of items, showing their stock status and value [S3].

In summary, `inventory.ts` defines the foundational data model and key functions that are consumed by `pricing.ts` and `report.ts`, enabling the system to calculate prices and generate reports based on stock conditions.
